books.author: gabriel-garcia-marquez
books.theme_zh: 魔幻现实主义的顶点：布恩迪亚家族七代人的循环史，如何把拉美的孤独写成一种结构
books.theme_en: The summit of magical realism: how the Buendía family's seven generations turn Latin America's solitude into a structure

prose.description_zh: 加西亚·马尔克斯 1967 年出版的长篇，讲述虚构小镇马孔多上布恩迪亚家族七代人的兴衰。马孔多从吉普赛人带来的磁铁与冰块起步，经历殖民屠杀、香蕉公司屠杀、罢工、连绵内战与久旱不歇的雨，最后被飓风抹去。开篇写家族奠基者带着整条血脉迁入马孔多，把姓名与命运刻在墙上的白灰里；全书写的则是孤独如何从一个人的执念变成家族的宿命，再变成一个国家的处境：四代人反复使用同样的名字，重复同样的冲动，誓愿与失败彼此复制。叙事者面对飞升上校与飞毯这类奇事时保持不惊讶的口吻，超自然与日常被放在同一层面上叙述，这就是魔幻现实主义。书的结尾，家族最后一位读者在羊皮卷上读到自己的命运，正被蚂蚁吃掉、被雨淋湿，而雨停了。
prose.description_en: Published in 1967, Gabriel García Márquez's novel follows seven generations of the Buendía family in the fictional town of Macondo. The town begins with the magnets and ice blocks brought by gypsies, passes through colonial massacres, the banana company massacre, strikes, endless civil war and a rain that will not stop, and is finally erased by a hurricane. The opening has the founder of the line settle in Macondo with his whole descendants and inscribe names and fates into the whitewash of the walls; what the book then traces is how solitude moves from one man's obsession to a family curse to a national condition, four generations reusing the same names and repeating the same impulses, vows and defeats copying each other. The narrating voice stays unastonished before events like the Colonel's ascension and the flying carpets, so that the supernatural and the ordinary are reported on the same plane. That is magical realism. The novel ends with the last reader of the family deciphering his own destiny on a parchment while ants carry him off and the rain stops.
prose.why_read_zh: 这本书提供的不是故事，而是一台解释机器：把「一个共同体如何重复自己的起源」变成可分析的模型。马孔多的每一次灾难都有对应的政治原因，但书真正追问的是，为什么后人无法从历史里学到东西——上校发起的三十二场战争全部失败，子孙继续发动同样的战争，因为家族没有发展出记忆，只有重复。反直觉之处在于，魔幻现实主义并不是把神话塞进现实，而是反过来：荒诞之所以被当作日常接受，恰恰因为现实本身已经足够荒诞，所以叙述者才不必惊讶。这一立场可被严肃反驳：批评者指出作品在殖民与屠杀叙事上的失焦、对女性角色的处理，以及它把拉美历史收束进单一家族谱系的封闭性——从香蕉园里士兵用机枪屠戮工人，到家族内部对子女的压抑，暴力并不总是宏大的，常常就在家庭内部。可迁移的框架是「循环史观」：当一个家族的姓名、症状与誓言代代复现，问题就不在个人，而在没有记忆的结构；而结构是可以被检视的，这正是这本书留给读者的提问方式。经典性证据（命中 6 项）：① 豆瓣读书《百年孤独》（[哥伦比亚] 加西亚·马尔克斯 / 范晔 / 南海出版公司 / 2011-6 / ISBN 9787544253994）评分 9.3 分、482,914 人评价，达到「评分 ≥8.5 且评价人数 ≥1000」门槛；② Goodreads 英文版 One Hundred Years of Solitude 评分 4.13 分、1,164,468 人评分（65,847 条书评），达到「评分 ≥4.0 且评分人数 ≥5000」门槛；③ 英文维基百科有独立条目 One Hundred Years of Solitude，载明 1967 年 5 月于阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯 Editorial Sudamericana 初版、原始语言为西班牙语，并说明魔幻现实主义（magical realism）一词由德国艺术批评家 Franz Roh 于 1925 年提出、本书是该流派的代表作品；④ 权威奖项：作者加西亚·马尔克斯于 1982 年获诺贝尔文学奖，该条目收录其获奖演讲中「This, my friends, is the crux of our solitude.」一语；⑤ 微信读书推荐值 89.4%、8.3 万人点评，达到 ≥80% 门槛；⑥ 课程采用：超星慕课「《百年孤独》精读」以本书为唯一阅读对象（2024-2025 学年春季学期开课，通识选修，16 学时），国外多所高校课程亦以本书为拉美小说单元首讲（Athabasca University ENGL 458 The Latin American Novel 单元一；University of Warsaw 3305-PLA-OG The Latin American Novel 第二周；Westminster College IC 102: Reading the World Gabriel García Márquez 全课核心）。未计入项：豆瓣不同版本快照评分 9.1–9.6、评价人数 31,760–482,914 不一，统一以评价人数最多的南海出版公司 2011 年范晔译本快照（subject/6082808）为口径，不并用其他版本数据；Goodreads 西语原版 Cien años de soledad 评分 4.12、1,147,767 人评分，数值接近英文版，未并用。时间检验：1967 年初版，至 2026-11-27 已满 59 年，远超 ≥5 年门槛。
prose.why_read_en: The book supplies not a story but an explanatory machine: it turns the question of how a community repeats its own origins into something that can be analysed. Every catastrophe in Macondo has a political cause, but what the book actually asks is why later generations cannot learn from history. The Colonel's thirty-two wars all fail, and his descendants keep starting the same wars, because the family develops no memory, only repetition. The counterintuitive move is that magical realism does not insert myth into reality; it is the other way round. The absurd is accepted as ordinary precisely because reality has become absurd enough, which is why the narrator is not required to be astonished. The position is open to serious objection, and has been: critics point to the book's loss of focus on colonial and massacre history, to its treatment of women, and to the closure of condensing Latin American history into a single family genealogy, since the violence is not always macro-political but often domestic, as with the sons' suppression of their own children. The portable frame is the cyclical reading of history: when names, symptoms and vows recur across generations, the problem lies not in individuals but in a structure without memory. And a structure, unlike a person, can be examined. That is the question the book leaves the reader holding. Classic evidence (six items matched): (1) the Douban edition 百年孤独 ([哥伦比亚] 加西亚·马尔克斯 / 范晔 / 南海出版公司 / 2011-6, ISBN 9787544253994) scores 9.3 from 482,914 raters, clearing the 8.5-and-1,000 bar; (2) Goodreads gives the English One Hundred Years of Solitude 4.13 from 1,164,468 ratings (65,847 reviews), clearing the 4.0-and-5,000 bar; (3) English Wikipedia carries a standalone article on One Hundred Years of Solitude recording the May 1967 first publication by Editorial Sudamericana in Buenos Aires, Argentina, the Spanish original, and the point that the term magical realism was coined by the German critic Franz Roh in 1925, with this novel among its representative works; (4) a major prize, the author García Márquez won the 1982 Nobel Prize in Literature and the article quotes his acceptance speech: This, my friends, is the crux of our solitude; (5) WeChat Reading shows a recommendation value of 89.4% across 83,000 comments, above the 80% threshold; (6) curriculum adoption, the Chaoxing MOOC course 《百年孤独》精读 is built around this single book as a general-education elective of 16 hours in the spring 2024-2025 term, and comparable courses at several universities open their Latin American novel units with it (Athabasca University ENGL 458 The Latin American Novel, Unit 1; University of Warsaw 3305-PLA-OG The Latin American Novel, Week 2; Westminster College IC 102: Reading the World Gabriel García Márquez, where it occupies most of the term). Not counted: Douban snapshots for other editions range from 9.1 to 9.6 with 31,760 to 482,914 raters, so the single snapshot with the largest rater count (the Nan Hai 2011 Fan Yi translation, subject 6082808) is used as the basis instead of pooling; the Spanish original Cien años de soledad shows 4.12 from 1,147,767 raters on Goodreads, close to the English figures, so it is not counted separately. Age test: first published in 1967, fifty-nine years before 2026-11-27, well beyond the five-year threshold.
core_ideas_zh: 魔幻现实主义不是把神话塞进现实，而是把荒诞当作日常来叙述：马孔多的居民对飞升的地毯和失眠症瘟疫习以为常，因为现实本身已经足够荒诞
循环史观：家族四代共用姓名、重复同一种冲动与誓言，说明没有记忆的结构才会让失败一遍遍上演——上校的三十二场战争与子孙的续演互为镜像
孤独是一种被制造出来的处境，而非天生的孤独：建村这个最初的执念（与外界隔绝以建起自己的世界）后来成了整个家族与整个小镇的宿命
可被反驳之处：批评者指出其对殖民屠杀与香蕉公司屠杀的叙事失焦、对女性角色的处理，以及用单一家族谱系收束拉美历史的封闭性
core_ideas_en: Magical realism does not insert myth into reality but reports the absurd as ordinary: Macondo's inhabitants are accustomed to flying carpets and a plague of insomnia because reality has itself become absurd enough

A cyclical view of history: four generations share names and repeat the same impulses and vows, which is what shows that a structure without memory makes failure recur, the Colonel's thirty-two wars and his descendants' reenactments mirroring each other

Solitude is a made condition rather than an innate one: the founding obsession, a settlement sealed off from the world to build a world of its own, becomes the fate of the whole family and the whole town

Refutable: critics point to the book's loss of focus on colonial and massacre history, to its treatment of women, and to the closure of condensing Latin American history into a single family genealogy
key_questions_zh: 一个共同体怎样才能打破「用同一个名字重复同一种失败」的循环：需要的是记忆、制度，还是别的什么？
当奇事被当作日常接受，我们该用什么标准判断一个社会已经越过了正常的边界？
家族叙事能不能承载一个国家的历史，还是必然在第三代人就开始失真？
key_questions_en: How can a community break the cycle of repeating the same failure under the same names: does it take memory, institutions, or something else?
When extraordinary events are accepted as ordinary, by what standard do we judge that a society has already crossed the boundary of the normal?
Can a family narrative carry the history of a country, or must it begin to distort by the third generation?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 适合想读一部能反复重读、且每次能读出新东西的小说的人：第一次读会跟着故事走，读第二遍才会注意到结构。同时适合对拉美历史、殖民与屠杀叙事感兴趣的人，以及需要理解「集体记忆如何失效」的读者——家族史、平台数据、组织文化其实是同一个问题。写作者尤其该读：它示范了如何用具体细节承载抽象主题。提醒一句：第一次读很容易被几十个相似姓名劝退，先准备一张人物关系表或直接读范晔译本的章节脉络会好很多。
prose.who_should_read_en: For anyone who wants a novel that can be reread and yields something different each time: a first reading follows the story, and only a second reading reveals the structure. It also suits readers interested in Latin American history, colonialism and massacre narratives, and anyone who needs to understand how collective memory fails, since family history, platform data and organisational culture are the same problem. Writers in particular should read it, for the demonstration of how concrete detail carries an abstract theme. One warning: dozens of similar names are a genuine obstacle on a first reading, so prepare a relationship chart or follow the chapter arc of the Fan Yi translation and the going will be easier.
prose.reading_note_zh: 建议分两遍。第一遍通读全书，只管跟着马孔多的兴衰走，不必记住每个人；读到结尾羊皮卷那段再回头。第二遍才做两件事：把四代同名者排成一张表，看名字如何复用、症结如何继承；再把上校的三十二场战争与香蕉公司屠杀对照读，看失败被归因于何处。若想读得更省力，可以先读马尔克斯的《活着为了讲述》，了解他如何把外祖母的讲述当作素材源头；若想读得更深，读完可接《霍乱时期的爱情》，看同一套魔幻语法如何处理爱情这一最难的对象，或读卡尔维诺谈马尔克斯的评论，检验自己的判断。
prose.reading_note_en: Read it in two passes. The first is straight through: follow the rise and fall of Macondo without trying to hold on to every character, and go back to the closing pages on the parchment once you reach them. The second pass does two things: lay out the four generations of shared names in a chart to watch names recur and symptoms get inherited, and set the Colonel's thirty-two wars against the banana company massacre to see where failure gets assigned. If you want an easier entry, read Vivir para contarla first to see how the author turned his grandmother's storytelling into raw material; if you want to go deeper afterwards, follow with El amor en los tiempos del cólera to see the same magical grammar applied to love, the hardest subject of all, or read Calvino on Márquez and test your own judgement.

books.title_zh: 编码：隐匿在计算机软硬件背后的语言
books.title_en: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
books.author: charles-petzold
books.theme_zh: 从手电筒到操作系统逐层重建一台计算机：编码、通信与「聪明人走过的死路」
books.theme_en: Rebuilding a computer layer by layer from a flashlight to the operating system: encoding, communication, and the dead ends smart people took

prose.description_zh: 查尔斯·佩措尔德 1999 年由 Microsoft Press 出版的科普书，2012 年由电子工业出版社引进中文版（左飞、薛佟佟译）。全书按计算机的层级自下而上重建：先讲编码与组合——摩尔斯电码、布莱叶盲文为何都需要最少两种符号；再讲二进制与逻辑门，从继电器、电灯泡一路搭到与门、或门、异或门；然后用这些门造出加法机、触发器、时钟与存储器，组成一台微处理器；最后讲总线、ASCII、操作系统、浮点数、编程语言与图形界面。作者反复采用同一个手法：不直接给出结论，而是先搭出前一层，再用它解释后一层的由来，例如「为什么计算机最终选了二进制而不是十进制」这个决定来自 von Neumann 结构，而非来自算术本身。全书配有大量手绘电路图，章节之间是严格的依赖关系，前一章不读后一章会读不懂。
prose.description_en: A popular science book published by Microsoft Press in 1999, translated into Chinese by the Publishing House of Electronics Industry in 2012. Charles Petzold rebuilds a computer layer by layer. He begins with encoding and combination, asking why Morse code and Braille both need at least two symbols; then binary and logic gates, moving from relays and light bulbs to AND, OR and XOR gates; then assembling those gates into an adding machine, flip-flops, a clock and memory, and from them a microprocessor; and finally buses, ASCII, the operating system, floating point, programming languages and the graphical interface. The method is consistent throughout: rather than asserting a conclusion, he builds the previous layer and then uses it to explain where the next one came from, which is why the choice of binary over decimal is explained as a consequence of the von Neumann architecture rather than of arithmetic itself. The volume is heavily illustrated with hand-drawn circuit diagrams, and its chapters form a strict dependency chain: skip one and the next will not make sense.
prose.why_read_zh: 这本书的真正价值是提供一套可以迁移的思维模型：任何复杂系统都可以按层级自下而上重建，每一层的存在都要由下一层的约束来解释。把「计算机能做什么」换成「计算机如何可能」，这是认知上的换挡。更反直觉的是它对「聪明人走死路」的处理：十进制计算机、机械计算机、按人的习惯设计的编码方案，在当时都显得更自然，但作者指出正是这些看似更聪明的方案不可扩展，最终胜出的二进制加 von Neumann 结构不是因为它更优雅，而是因为它更容易被搭出来——「聪明人」的错误不在于不够聪明，而在于过早优化了错误的目标。这条教训对当下的 AI 热潮格外锋利：几乎所有生成式模型都建立在同一套 von Neumann 继承下来的架构上，我们正身处那本书所说的「聪明人走到死路」的又一次现场。它可被严肃反驳：全书以单机、个人计算为背景，分布式系统、现代 GPU 架构、量子计算、以及它明确回避的网络内容都不在讨论范围内；也有读者认为它与其说是科普，不如说是一本带插图的计算机科学本科教材，逐章推进、前后依赖，读起来并不轻松。经典性证据（命中 5 项）：① 豆瓣读书《编码：隐匿在计算机软硬件背后的语言》（[美] Charles Petzold / 左飞 / 薛佟佟 / 电子工业出版社 / 2012-10 / ISBN 9787121181184 / 420 页）评分 9.2 分、1,002 人评价，达到「评分 ≥8.5 且评价人数 ≥1000」门槛；② Goodreads 英文版 Code 评分 4.40 分、10,961 人评分（915 条书评），达到「评分 ≥4.0 且评分人数 ≥5000」门槛；③ 英文维基百科有独立条目 Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software，载明 1999 年 9 月 29 日由 Microsoft Press 出版、393 页、ISBN 0-7356-0505-X，并说明本书已被纳入高校「Fundamentals of Modern Software」等入门及中级计算机科学与工程课程的教学大纲；④ 权威书评媒体：Publishers Weekly 在出版后即刊出书评，出版社编辑 Ben Ryan 称其意图「跨越计算机书类的边界，把 Code 作为一般性非虚构科学推出」，并称其叙述清晰易懂；⑤ 中文版正式出版并获名校推荐：机械工业出版社 2025 年第 2 版中文本（张建锋译，ISBN 9787111785095）封面载明「麻省理工、斯坦福、哈佛等名校重磅推荐」。未计入项：豆瓣存在多个版本快照，电子工业出版社 2012 年版评分 9.2 / 1,002 人，机械工业出版社 2025 年第 2 版评分另见其他快照，两者不并用，统一以年代较早、评价人数可核验的 2012 年版为口径；Goodreads 法文版评分 4.40 / 10,855 人评分，与英文版数值接近，未并用。时间检验：1999 年初版，至 2026-11-27 已满 27 年，远超 ≥5 年门槛。
prose.why_read_en: The book's real value is a transferable model: any complicated system can be rebuilt layer by layer from the bottom, and the existence of each layer has to be explained by the constraints of the one beneath it. Replacing the question of what a computer can do with the question of how a computer is even possible is a change of gear in cognition. The counterintuitive part is the book's treatment of the dead ends taken by smart people. Decimal computing, mechanical computing, and encoding schemes designed the way human beings are accustomed to think all looked more natural at the time, yet the author shows that these apparently cleverer approaches would not scale, and that binary plus the von Neumann architecture won not because it was more elegant but because it was easier to build. The error of the clever people was not insufficient cleverness but optimising the wrong target early, and that lesson lands with particular force in the current AI excitement, since nearly every generative model runs on an architecture inherited from von Neumann and we are standing inside another instance of the dead end the book describes. The book is open to serious objection: it is framed entirely around the single machine and personal computing, and distributed systems, modern GPU architectures, quantum computing and networking are all outside its scope, the author stating that he focused on pre-networked computers because distributed computing would not be useful for most people using the Internet. Some readers argue it is less a popular science book than an illustrated undergraduate textbook in computer science, strictly sequential and dependent, and not an easy read. Classic evidence (five items matched): (1) the Douban edition 编码：隐匿在计算机软硬件背后的语言 ([美] Charles Petzold / 左飞 / 薛佟佟 / 电子工业出版社 / 2012-10, ISBN 9787121181184, 420 pages) scores 9.2 from 1,002 raters, clearing the 8.5-and-1,000 bar; (2) Goodreads gives the English Code 4.40 from 10,961 ratings (915 reviews), clearing the 4.0-and-5,000 bar; (3) English Wikipedia carries a standalone article on Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software recording its 29 September 1999 publication by Microsoft Press, 393 pages, ISBN 0-7356-0505-X, and noting that it has been included in the syllabi of post-secondary technical courses such as Fundamentals of Modern Software, as well as other introductory and mid-level computer science and engineering courses; (4) an authoritative review outlet, Publishers Weekly carried a review shortly after publication, in which the book's editor Ben Ryan says the aim was to cross the boundary of the computer section and break out Code as general nonfiction science, and praises the writing as clear and easy to understand; (5) a formal Chinese edition carrying institutional recommendations, the Machine Press second Chinese edition (2025, translated by Zhang Jianfeng, ISBN 9787111785095) states on its cover that it is recommended by institutions including MIT, Stanford and Harvard. Not counted: Douban snapshots for different editions differ, with the 2012 Publishing House of Electronics Industry edition at 9.2 from 1,002 raters and the 2025 Machine Press second edition scoring differently in other snapshots, so the older edition with the verifiable rater count is used as the basis instead of pooling; the French edition shows 4.40 from 10,855 raters on Goodreads, close to the English figures, so it is not counted separately. Age test: first published in 1999, twenty-seven years before 2026-11-27, well beyond the five-year threshold.
core_ideas_zh: 编码是信息处理的起点：任何符号系统只要用最少两种符号加上组合规则就能承载复杂含义，二进制并非因为计算机「擅长算二」而被选中
自下而上重建：先造出加法机、触发器、时钟与存储器，再组成微处理器——每一层的存在都由下一层的约束来解释，而不是先有结论再补解释
聪明人的死路：十进制与机械方案看起来更自然却不可扩展，二进制加 von Neumann 架构胜出是因为更容易被搭出来，教训不在不够聪明而在过早优化了错误的目标
可被反驳之处：全书以单机与个人计算为背景，明确回避分布式与网络内容；有读者认为它更像带插图的计算机科学本科教材，严格依赖、并不好读
core_ideas_en: Encoding comes first in the handling of information: any symbol system needs as few as two symbols plus rules of combination to carry complex meaning, and binary was not chosen because computers are good at arithmetic in base two

Rebuilding from the bottom: the adding machine, the flip-flops, the clock and the memory come first, and only then the microprocessor, with each layer explained by the constraints of the one beneath rather than asserted and illustrated afterwards

The dead ends of clever people: decimal and mechanical schemes looked more natural yet would not scale, and binary plus the von Neumann architecture won because it was easier to build, so the lesson is not insufficient cleverness but optimising the wrong target too early

Refutable: the book is framed around the single machine and personal computing and deliberately leaves out distributed and networked systems, and some readers find it closer to an illustrated undergraduate textbook in computer science, strictly sequential and not an easy read
key_questions_zh: 一个复杂系统应该按什么顺序被拆解：先问它能做什么，还是先问它如何可能？
当一个方案在直觉上更自然却难以扩展时，我们凭什么判断它走错了路？
今天几乎所有主流计算架构都来自同一场历史选择，我们今天正在复制的那条「聪明人的死路」会出现在哪里？
key_questions_en: In what order should a complicated system be taken apart: should one first ask what it can do, or first ask how it is possible at all?
When an approach feels more natural yet resists scaling, on what grounds do we judge that it has gone down the wrong road?
Almost every mainstream computing architecture descends from a single historical choice, so where will the next instance of the clever people's dead end appear?
prose.who_should_read_zh: 适合任何自认「知道计算机能做什么、但不知道为什么」的人：文科背景想理解 AI 的读者、想补上底层直觉的产品与投资研究者、正在入门编程但总在抽象层打转的学生。它也是给技术从业者的提醒——当所有人都在同一套架构上加参数时，回头看那本书为什么从手电筒讲起，会让人重新判断什么才算「新」。反过来，如果你要的是可立即照做的工程手册，它帮不上忙；它讲的是原理与由来，不是做法。
prose.who_should_read_en: For anyone who knows what a computer can do but not why: readers from non-technical backgrounds trying to understand AI, product and investment researchers who want the underlying intuition, and students starting to program who keep circling at the level of abstraction. It is also a warning to people already in the trade: when everyone adds parameters to the same architecture, going back to why the book begins with a flashlight is a way to re-evaluate what counts as new. If what you want is an engineering manual you can apply on Monday, it will not help; it is about principles and origins, not procedures.
prose.reading_note_zh: 按顺序读，不要跳章——章节之间是严格依赖的，前一章不读后一章会读不懂。最省力的读法是边读边画图：每读完一章，用纸笔把这一层的输入输出与它下一层的关系画成方框图，三十页之后你手上会有一张完整的计算机分层图，也就不需要回头看原书插图了。可以配合的两个外部参照：一是《计算机程序的构造和解释》，它从语言层往上看，与本书自下而上的路径正好相反，两本对着读能校准你漏掉的层；二是任一本现代体系结构的入门教材，用来补上本书刻意不谈的并行与缓存。读完若想知道这套架构的时代局限，可接着读 2025 年机械工业出版社出版的原书第 2 版中文本，看作者如何重写 CPU 内部那一章。
prose.reading_note_en: Read it in order and do not skip chapters, since they form a strict dependency chain and a chapter you skip will make the next one unintelligible. The cheapest method is to draw as you read: after each chapter, sketch the inputs and outputs of that layer and its relation to the one below in boxes, and after some thirty pages you will hold a complete layered diagram of the computer and no longer need to turn back to the book's illustrations. Two external references work well alongside it: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs, which looks downward from the language layer and thus takes the opposite path from this bottom-up build, so reading the two against each other will calibrate the layer you have missed; and any introductory text on modern architecture, to supply the parallelism and caching this book pointedly leaves out. To see the limits of this architecture's moment afterwards, read the second Chinese edition published by Machine Press in 2025 and note how the author rewrites the chapter on the inside of the CPU.
